summary:
Developed by Team GalaSEE for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, TideAware is a real-time mangrove monitoring system designed for the Cần Giờ mangrove forest in Vietnam. It integrates NISAR L-band SAR satellite data with a physics-guided AI pipeline to remove tidal interference.
The primary challenge in radar-based forestry monitoring is that significant tidal fluctuations create double-bounce reflections, producing widespread false-positive flood and deforestation alerts. TideAware directly addresses this by incorporating real-time water level data and tidal gating to separate natural cyclical water changes from true ecological disturbances.
This system is critical because it filters out observation noise, ensures high algorithmic reliability, and accurately pinpoints genuine high-risk degradation zones. By doing so, TideAware optimizes inspection routes for rangers and strengthens the long-term protection of vulnerable coastal ecosystems.
details:
1. Project Overview & Core Motivation Developed by Team GalaSEE for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, TideAware is an advanced, real-time mangrove monitoring system specifically designed for the Cần Giờ mangrove forest in Vietnam. While mangrove ecosystems serve as vital ecological buffers and natural carbon sinks, monitoring their health using synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite data faces a major hydrodynamic obstacle: extreme tidal fluctuations (reaching up to 3.5 to 4.0 meters). These massive water-level changes induce severe double-bounce radar backscatter variations, which traditional remote sensing models frequently misinterpret as false-positive flood events, sudden biomass losses, or deforestation. TideAware solves this critical bottleneck by merging high-resolution NISAR L-band SAR data with a rigorous, physics-guided machine learning pipeline.

2. System Architecture & 4-Layer Workflow TideAware operates through a robust, automated four-layer processing pipeline that bridges oceanographic physics with deep learning:

  • Layer 1 (Data Ingestion & AOI Cropping): Automatically acquires NISAR L2 GCOV HDF5 scenes from the ASF Data Pool via secure token authentication, crops them precisely to the Cần Giờ Area of Interest (AOI) under the UTM Zone 48N coordinate system, and converts raw power values into decibel units. An efficient streaming workflow ensures memory-efficient processing on cloud environments.
  • Layer 2 (Physics-Guided Tide Correction): Integrates real-time water level data from local tidal stations combined with harmonic water analysis. It applies an Empirical Bayes regression model per pixel to estimate tide sensitivity coefficients and dynamic time-lag parameters, mathematically isolating and removing cyclical water-level variations.
  • Layer 3 (Spatiotemporal AI Feature Extraction): Feeds the cleaned SAR backscatter, physical expectations, normalized residuals, and tidal dynamics into a lightweight Spatiotemporal Attention Encoder. This deep learning module learns complex biomass degradation patterns that remain invariant to natural tidal cycles.
  • Layer 4 (Persistent Change Detection & Alert Generation): Applies a Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) change detection algorithm coupled with a strict temporal persistence rule across consecutive observation cycles. This successfully eliminates transient weather and storm-induced noise, producing clean, high-confidence degradation maps exported as structured geospatial data.

3. Key Benefits & Practical Impact

  • Elimination of False Alarms: Explicitly accounts for oceanographic physics, preventing natural tides from triggering false deforestation or flood alerts.
  • Operational Efficiency for Conservation: Empowers local forestry management and rangers by pinpointing true high-risk degradation zones, significantly optimizing field patrol routes and resource allocation.
  • Global Scalability: The modular physics-informed architecture can be readily adapted to monitor tidal wetlands, estuaries, and coastal mangrove forests worldwide.
